card: Adds btck_witness_stack_get_items and a C++ wrapper method WitnessStackApi::GetItems to libbitcoinkernel. Under the compact serialized witness stack representation proposed in base PR 36895, indexing an item requires walking preceding items, causing full-stack reads via btck_witness_stack_get_item_at to run in O(n^2) time. This API parses the entire stack in a single O(n) pass, outputting pointers and sizes into arrays so callers can read items in any order. Depends on #36895.
changed_since_previous: Replaced the callback-based iterator btck_witness_stack_iterate_items with btck_witness_stack_get_items (and WitnessStackApi::GetItems). Instead of executing a callback for each item in bottom-up order, it writes all pointers and sizes into output arrays, allowing callers to inspect items in any order.
evidence: PR description: 'Reading a whole witness stack with btck_witness_stack_get_item_at is O(n^2) because each call walks the items before the one it returns. This function gets every item in one O(n) pass and the caller can read them in any order.'
problem: Under the serialized witness stack representation introduced in #36895, indexing into a witness stack requires walking all preceding items and takes O(n) time. External consumers reading an entire witness stack through repeated calls to `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` therefore face an O(n^2) runtime penalty.

risk.why: A memory or indexing bug in the new kernel API function could cause out-of-bounds reads or crashes for external consumers of libbitcoinkernel.

scope_notes: Only the final commit belongs to this pull request. The preceding 13 commits refactoring CScriptWitness to store witness stacks in serialized form belong to base PR #36895.
summary: Adds `btck_witness_stack_get_items` and a C++ wrapper method `WitnessStackApi::GetItems` to the libbitcoinkernel API. The function parses a witness stack in a single linear pass and writes each item's pointer and length into caller-supplied arrays. This enables kernel consumers to access all stack items in O(n) time and read them in any order without repeatedly traversing the serialization.
